question: Cash machines spread through American banks from the 1980s. What happened to the number of human cashiers working in them?
answer: Kept growing slowly. Machines cut the tellers an average urban branch needed from 20 to 13 between 1988 and 2004. That made branches cheaper to run, so banks opened 43% more of them. Fewer tellers per branch, more branches: the job moved from counting cash to selling services across the counter.
move: A machine that makes a task cheap can create more of the work around it.
ask: If a machine made the dullest part of my job cheap, what would the rest of my work become?
trap: Assuming each machine simply replaced the person whose task it did.
